Subject: FinServCo - Eval plan and next steps

Thanks again for the call today, Alex — great context on the reconciliation use case and the throughput requirements. Recap below plus proposed next steps for running customer-specific evals on Redwood. Please reply with any clarifications or the sample dataset when you have it.

Summary of fit / recommended model choices
- Primary model: rwd-llama-65b-quant (recommended for good quality / cost balance on transactional text)
- Fallback: rwd-mistral-33b for lower latency legs during high throughput tests
- If strict latency SLOs are required (sub-200ms p50 for single-turn queries), we can evaluate a trimmed quantized variant and benchmark with your average sequence length.

Benchmarks and prompt sets
- We'll run both closed-book generation benchmarks (API prompt/response) and retrieval-augmented generation tests against your knowledge snippets.
- I'll share our baseline benchmark report and prompt-set templates: see Redwood eval guide (link below).

Dataset & format requirements (how to prepare sample upload)
- Preferred format: CSV UTF-8, comma-separated. Required columns: id, input_text, reference_output, metadata_json (optional).
- For multiple-turn cases: include a conversation_history column containing newline-separated turns, and a turn_index to indicate which turn is being evaluated.
- Labels: reference_output should be the expected output string. For binary correctness tests, add a label column with values {correct,incorrect}.

Scoring & evaluation criteria
- Generation quality: exact-match and normalized-EM where applicable; token-level F1 for information-extraction tasks; BLEU/ROUGE only for longer summarization-like outputs.
- Safety/regression checks: run our prompt-safety suite (we'll include the default rules) and a delta vs. your current baseline model. We'll surface any quality regressions by prompt set and by example.

Operational setup on Redwood
- Option A (hosted): share a secure S3 location or upload sample CSV to the Redwood Console -> Evaluations tab; we'll pull and run the harness.
- Option B (Private/VPC): we can run evals inside your VPC; we'll provide instructions for a temporary job runner and a signed upload endpoint.

Next steps (action items)
1) Alex: share a sample dataset (100-500 rows) with a couple of edge-case examples — see required columns above.
2) Neha/Dev: prep an eval config (model list, metrics, bucket/namespace) after Alex sends sample.
3) Marissa: follow up with benchmark links and a proposed 30/60-min technical setup slot.

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.md (template for eval config), example CSV column snapshot included below.

Example CSV header: id,input_text,conversation_history,reference_output,label,metadata_json

Feel free to ping me directly with any constraints around PII, retention, or redaction needs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Hey Alex — thanks for sending the sample, looks useful. Quick technical notes (copied from our eval playbook):

1) Normalization & scoring
- We recommend you provide normalized references for numeric values if exact numeric equality is required; otherwise we'll apply Redwood's numeric normalizer (strip thousands separators, map USD symbols to plain numbers) before computing token-F1. Call out "exact_numeric=true" in the eval metadata if you want strict equality.

2) Conversation delimiter
- Newline is preferred; if your dataset uses pipe (|), we'll accept it but please indicate "turn_delim=|" in the eval config so tokenization lines up.

3) Eval config (high-level)
- model_candidates: [rwd-llama-65b-quant, rwd-mistral-33b]
- metrics: [normalized_em, token_f1, safety_checks, latency_p50, latency_p95]
- scoring_rules: "normalize_numbers:true;case_insensitive:true"

4) Handling PII
- Good to mask account numbers; for any fields needing redaction we recommend providing a mapping file (id -> redaction_token) in metadata_json. We will not retain raw uploads beyond the eval retention window unless you request it.

5) Expected turnaround
- Baseline eval run (150 rows) on hosted Redwood: ~24-48 hours after dataset upload and config finalization. Private runs may need additional infra provisioning (add ~1-2 business days).

6) Deliverables
- Per-example scores, aggregated metric table, regression diffs vs. your baseline model, and a short summary deck.

If you want, Dev and I can run a smoke test on a 20-row subset first to validate config. When's a good time for a quick 30-min tech setup?
